items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: When you came up here in 2005 to play with Kenny

ctx.x: Well it’s been affected by pick-ups and, you know the high-tech method of recording to a certain extent. I was just listening to a couple of Chet Baker records recorded in Italy with these bizarre mixes and it sounded like they were just recording the bass through a pick-up that sounded like a banjo you know. But the bass has not changed. I have a bass that’s 280 years old, one of my basses, and it’s got the same — the sound improves year by year by aging. And a contractor called me up recently about a show that…

When you came up here in 2005 to play with Kenny — and I recall that you didn’t want an amplifier, the room was acoustically really wonderful, but do you find that your fellow musicians on a club date or something play differently volume-wise when you don’t have an amplifier? Are they sympathetic to your bass set-up?

It’s a great question because I believe that the bass really affects the balance of a band or an orchestra. And one reason I got away from amplifying was because if you use a pick- up and you bow it sounds like a baritone sax you know. So you have to get a full tone with no amp.
